title: mentha arvensis subsp. borealis
intro: Mentha arvensis subsp. borealis, commonly known as Japanese peppermint, is a subspecies of the mint plant that is native to North America and parts of Asia. It is known for its health benefits, which include reducing nausea and digestive issues, as well as its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Japanese peppermint include its ability to ease respiratory issues such as coughs and colds, as well as its use in aromatherapy for relaxation and stress relief. The bioactive constituents of Japanese peppermint include menthol, menthone, and limonene, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
